findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The top of the inside of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on the sides. CORRECTED- One of the PICs cleaned this during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned regularly and maintained clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to fill a container in the handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated and aware that handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a container of raw salmon above a container of cooked beef in the bottom of a preparation cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the PIC corrected the storage order (the salmon was moved below the beef in the cooler). Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The walk-in cooler fan has a leak coming from it that the PIC stated had just started today. The PIC discarded food items that were under it and moved others to protect them from contamination. Bins were placed under the leak until it can be repaired. The PIC stated that the walk-in cooler might be in defrost mode. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Inspector observed a staff member shutting off the sink without using a barrier after handwashing. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff members remember to use a barrier after to shut off the faucet in order to avoid recontaminating their hands. 


Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: THIS IS A THRICE REPEAT VIOLATION. There was no sanitizer bucket (s) available on the cook line at the beginning of today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. The sani bucket was made immediately. The final measured of the sanitizer concentration was 200 ppm. Ensure that sani buckets are made at the appropriate temperature at all times during food prep.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Inspector observed several food items in the walk-in cooler not properly date marked. Some of the items are but not limited to an opened jug of milk, sauces, dumplings fillings, cooked meat, and etc. PIC was made aware and education was carried out. Ensure that all food items are properly dated when they are being stored for future use. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION.The caulking on the handwashing sink by the pass through window at the front of the cook line was observed in disrepair. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the above mentioned handwashing sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.113 Inspector observed multiple mop heads stored improperly in the utility sink. Education was carried out and the mop heads were stored properly. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a way that allows them to air dry and discourage the growth of bacterial cultures.

Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff donning gloves without washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to wash their hands in between tasks before donning gloves for food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: At the beginning of the inspection, inspector observed an employee’s cellphone being stored on the prep table next to the coffee table by the bar area. Discussed with PIC and the cellphone was removed and stored properly. Ensure that all personal items like phones are stored in adequate space to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

findings.comment:
4-601.11: Inspector observed a dirty dish at pantry shelves stored as clean. The plate was moved to the dish area for proper cleaning. The violation is considered corrected on site. Train employees to evaluate clean dishes for cleanliness before putting them on the shelf for use. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen to test at 0ppm of Quat sanitizer. The bucket was removed and remade.

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: Inspector observed two employee bags stored on the overhead shelf next to paper towels on the prep line. Ensure that personal belongings are stored properly. 

(A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The can opener at the facility is encrusted with dry food debris. The can opener was soaked, washed, rinsed and sanitized at the time of inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site. Wash the can opener at least once every 24 hours. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
A pan of pasta was left in the prep top on top of the other pans and was out of refrigeration for an undetermined amount of time. The pasta was discarded in the garbage. Take care to store food properly refrigerated. The violation is corrected on site. Do not store foods in the prep tops above the line. Maintain a good practice for refrigeration at all times. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The small chest freezer in the back storage area has thick frost and is no longer cleanable. Defrost the freezer.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
